=== Overview ===
It is located in the northern part of Kanazawa. Irrigation water runs near the torii at the front approach, where a monument honors the builder of the canal. The precinct is covered by dense woodland, with an uphill approach leading to the shrine buildings.

According to ''Ishikawa Prefecture Shrine Records,'' the enshrined deities are Hajikami-no-Kami and Sei-Hachiman-no-Kami.

However, a local monument lists many deities: Hajikami-no-Kami, {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}, {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}, {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hime-no-?kami}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sukunabikona-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|lt=Futsunushi-no-Kami|Q1107286|qid=Q1107286}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Yasakatome|ja|八坂刀売神|simple|Yasakatome|zh|八坂刀賣神|qid=Q9150392}}, and {{ill|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Kami}}.

There is also the Shoichii Hachimanyama Inari-sha within the precinct, and a sessha called Jinbeid? enshrining {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|de|Takenouchi no Sukune|es|Takenouchi no Sukune|fa|تاکنوشی نو سوکون|fr|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰|ko|다케우치노 스쿠네|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯅꯣꯎꯆꯤ ꯅꯣ ꯁꯨꯀꯨꯅꯦ|pt|Takenouchi no Sukune|zh|武內宿禰|qid=Q1073668}}.

According to chief priest Tajika Akitsugu, the shrine name comes from the old word "hajikami" for pungent things chewed with the teeth (ginger, wasabi, sansh?, etc.)<ref>{{Cite web|??|title='Nice to meet you! I am the chief priest of Hajikami Shrine'|url=https://ameblo.jp/hajikamijinja/entry-10288587952.html|website=Chief priest's blog|accessdate=2020-11-25|language=ja|date=2009-06-27}}</ref>.

It was moved to Tajika Hachiman-g? at the current site and became a combined shrine, then later renamed to its current name because Hajikami-no-Kami, with Senior Fourth Rank, was considered above Hachiman.

The original site was at Kogane Sh?zu in Shib? Takasaka-ch?, about 2 km further inland.

=== Kogane Sh?zu spring ===
At the old shrine site in Shib? Takasaka-ch?, the spring called Kogane Sh?zu is tied to a legend: during severe drought in the Nara period, the kuni no miyatsuko prayed at this shrine for rain. On the 37th day, sacred water sprang forth and saved the people. With little left to offer, they dedicated ginger, beginning the unique "ginger festival" still held each year on {{ill|June 15|ab|Рашәарамза 15|af|15 Junie|als|15. In the Edo period, restaurant owners from Kaga, Etch?, and Noto reportedly visited. Because of ginger's medicinal properties, it also became a place of healing worship. This continues today<ref>Nagatanien, active in ginger research/product development, registered June 15 as "Ginger Day" with the Japan Anniversary Association in connection with this grand festival.</ref>.

=== Access ===
* Hokutetsu Kanazawa Bus: from {{ill|Morimoto Station|it|Stazione di Morimoto|ja|森本駅|ko|모리모토역|zh|森本站|qid=Q5359635|lt=Morimoto Station}}, route 87 via Hachiman to Moto-Tsubata; get off at Hachiman stop, 3 min walk
** For the distant worship hall: route 87 via Futsukaichi to Moto-Tsubata; get off at Futsukaichi (free boarding section; can board/alight near main gate, but service is limited)
